title: Remove Parentheses From Sign Expression
description:
Given a valid algebraic expression string `s` consisting of single lowercase variables (`'a'`-`'z'`), `'+'`, `'-'`, `'('`, and `')'` (with no spaces and no consecutive binary operators outside parentheses; unary `'-'` may appear at the start of `s` or immediately after `'('`), remove all parentheses while preserving exact mathematical equivalence by propagating outer signs.

Return the simplified parenthesization-free string with no leading `'+'` sign (for example, `"-(a-b)"` becomes `"-a+b"`, and `"-(-a)"` becomes `"a"`).
constraints: s is a valid expression of lowercase letters 'a'-'z', '+', '-', '(', and ')' with at least one variable.
hints: Maintain a stack of active sign multipliers (+1 or -1), initialized with [1], along with a local sign variable for the operator immediately preceding the next term or '('.
When seeing '(', push (stack.top * localSign) and reset localSign to +1; on ')', pop the stack; on a variable, apply effectiveSign = stack.top * localSign.

examples.explanation: The outer minus negates b and double-negates (c+d), yielding "a-b+c+d".
Negating (a-b) flips 'a' to '-a' and '-b' to '+b', giving "-a+b".
Two nested negations cancel on 'a', and leading '+' is omitted, yielding "a".
